title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB)
summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate remained flat at 3.65% as of April 14, 2026, unchanged from the prior observation on April 13. The rate has been constant at 3.65% from April 10 through April 14, 2026, indicating no change in the Fed's reserve remuneration policy during this period.
key_points: IORB rate held constant at 3.65% on April 14, 2026 (flat, no change from prior day)
Rate has been stable at 3.65% for at least 5 consecutive trading days (April 10-14, 2026)
Absolute change from previous observation: 0 basis points
IORB serves as the Fed's primary policy rate floor in the current operating framework
This rate represents the interest paid to depository institutions on reserve balances held at Federal Reserve Banks
why_it_matters: IORB is a critical component of the Fed's monetary policy operating framework. It functions as the floor for money market rates, directly influencing short-term borrowing costs throughout the financial system. Banks with excess reserves receive this rate from the Fed, which anchors the broader overnight lending markets (including repo and federal funds markets). The stability of IORB at 3.65% suggests the Fed is maintaining its current policy rate level without adjustment.
market_structure_context: IORB is central to the Fed's floor system operating framework, where reserves are abundant and the Fed pays interest on reserves to anchor the policy rate. The IORB rate sets a floor for money market rates; banks have no incentive to lend reserves below this rate in the federal funds or repo markets. This mechanism is key market structure infrastructure that transmits monetary policy to short-term funding markets.
notes: This is a point-in-time data observation from FRED, not a policy announcement. The flat IORB rate simply confirms the Fed's reserve remuneration rate is unchanged. No forward guidance or policy signals can be inferred from this observation alone. The IORB rate typically tracks close to or at the top of the Fed's target range (currently reflecting the 3.65% level consistent with the FOMC's 5.25%-5.50% target range midpoint).
